concepts.def: Two-class model: bourgeoisie own means of production, proletariat sell labour; objective class position drives conflict.
Class (market position), status (prestige) and party (power) are three dimensions of stratification.
1980 Nuffield study: seven-class scheme based on employment relations; basis of NS-SEC used by ONS.
Neo-Marxist: contradictory class locations (managers) hold authority but sell labour; expands Marx's binary.
Davis and Moore (1945): inequality is necessary to motivate the most talented to fill the most important positions.
Murray (1990): welfare-dependent group with deviant values; criticised for blaming victims of structural disadvantage.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Social Stratification & Differentiation — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Social Stratification & Differentiation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Social Stratification & Differentiation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
